02 · HORIZON LANDS

Where does reversal end — and momentum begin?

A raw 4-hour “momentum” signal prints Sharpe −3.58. That isn't momentum — it's a rubber band: mean reversion dominates everything up to 8 hours. Skip one bar to dodge the microstructure bounce, and the real signal appears — lagged momentum peaking at Sharpe 1.79 at the 12-hour mark.

03 · REVERSION FALLS

Fade the liquidation cascade

Abnormal volume marks forced selling — cascading liquidations, uninformed and exhausted. A six-day volume Z-score amplifies short-horizon reversal bets exactly when the snap-back is most violent. Before costs, it looks like a money machine.

gross Sharpe 3.58turnover 476×/yr
Source · Research notebook, Modules 4 & 6
04 · MOMENTUM RIDGE

Let medium-horizon winners keep running

A 21-day cross-sectional momentum signal, delayed one bar and rebalanced daily instead of every four hours. Slower, calmer, cheaper — persistent reallocation rather than microstructure noise.

gross Sharpe 1.36rebalanced dailysignal 21-day
Source · Research notebook, Modules 5 & 6
05 · THE COST CLIFF

The backtest meets the bid–ask spread

Reversion's 476× annual turnover is fatal: at realistic 7 bps limit-order costs, Sharpe 3.58 collapses to −1.32 net — the edge falls off the cliff. Momentum's calmer churn survives the fall: 1.36 → 1.02 net. Gross Sharpe is a rumor; net Sharpe is the truth.

06 · THE BLENDING SUMMIT

Diversification works — until the bill arrives

The two alphas correlate at ρ = −0.103 — a diversifier's dream. Gross mean–variance optimization agrees: a 40/60 blend reaches Sharpe 3.85. But net of costs, the optimizer refuses to pay for diversification it can't afford: the executable optimum is 100% momentum.

I built this statistical arbitrage system to understand where short-horizon reversal gives way to persistent momentum across liquid cryptocurrency markets. The research connected each empirical result to a market mechanism: liquidation cascades behind abrupt reversals, persistent reallocation behind medium-horizon trends, and microstructure bounce behind the noise in the latest four-hour bar. That evidence shaped the implementation. I delayed the signal by one bar, reduced the rebalance frequency, and evaluated every result after realistic transaction costs. The final daily-rebalanced strategy achieved a Net Sharpe of 1.02 with effectively zero beta to Bitcoin — a result driven by disciplined cross-sectional selection rather than a disguised directional bet.
— Ayan · Project reflection
